title: Satellite tracker

list.name: constellation
list.label: Constellation
list.description: Group of satellites, as defined in satapi/constellations.json. Loaded from the API's /constellations endpoint.

list.name: satellite
list.label: Satellite
list.description: One, several or All satellites in the selected constellation (from /satellites?group=...). The values are NORAD catalogue numbers; 'All' sends ids=all.

list.name: anim_seconds
list.label: Replay length (s)
list.description: How many seconds the replay of the selected time range takes.

list.name: label_limit
list.label: Label if ≤ N sats
list.description: Show satellite names on the map only when this many satellites or fewer are shown, so large constellations stay readable. 0 = never.

list.name: city
list.label: City
list.description: Observer location for the sky view. Choose 'Custom coordinates' to use the value of 'Custom lat, lon'.

list.name: coords
list.label: Custom lat, lon
list.description: Latitude, longitude in degrees (north and east positive), e.g. 42.70, 23.32. Used only when City = 'Custom coordinates'.

list.name: min_el
list.label: Min. elevation (°)
list.description: Hide satellites lower than this above the horizon in the sky view and the table (buildings and trees usually block the lowest 10°).

panels.title: Satellite motion — ${constellation}
panels.description: Replays the satellites' motion over the dashboard time range (maximum 24 h) in $anim_seconds seconds and stops at the range's end time. Blue dots: path travelled (25 or fewer satellites). Shading: night side, moving with the clock. Auto-refresh with an unchanged selection and range length updates the end positions without replaying; press ▶ (top right) to replay. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan. Data: query A, /animation. Code: grafana/panels/satellite-replay.js.

panels.title: Sky above ${city:text}
panels.description: The sky seen from the selected city or coordinates: zenith in the centre, horizon on the outer circle, North up and East on the left (as on a star chart held overhead). Satellites above the horizon move across it over the time range, like the map. Yellow: sunlit. Grey: in Earth's shadow, so invisible to the eye. Faint blue grid: celestial parallels (declination, every 30°, equator brighter) and meridians (right ascension, every 2 h). Faint lines: main constellations. The sky background brightens with the Sun's altitude. Data: A /sky, B /observer, C /sky_chart. Code: grafana/panels/sky-view.js.

panels.title: Above the horizon at the end time
panels.description: Satellites above the minimum elevation as seen from the selected place at the end of the time range (/visible), highest first. Azimuth: 0° = North, 90° = East.

panels.title: Current positions
panels.description: Current position of each selected satellite (/positions). 'Element set age' is how old the Space-Track orbital data is; older data means less accurate positions.

panels.title: Data status
panels.description: Number of satellites shown, median age of their orbital data (orange above 3 days, red above 7 days), and when the API last downloaded the constellation from Space-Track (/summary).

description: Satellite motion from Space-Track orbital data, propagated with SGP4 by the Python API (satapi). Pick a constellation and satellites at the top and a time range of up to 24 h: the map replays the motion over that range and stops at its end time ('now' = live). The table and status panels show the end time. See grafana/dashboards/README.md for how this file is built.
